title: BoNC: Discovering and Classifying Novel Encrypted Botnet Traffic
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society

label_source.evidence: The malicious scenarios were generated by executing specific malware samples in a controlled network environment.

label_feature_overlap.evidence: Ethernet, IP, and TCP header fields are stripped before feature extraction.

features_used.evidence: In this pre-training stage, each packet is limited to 64 bytes of data following the Ethernet layer to focus on meaningful payload information

feature_groups.evidence: A traffic burst is defined as a temporally contiguous sequence of packets transmitted in one direction (either client-to-server or server-to-client) within a single flow session

cert_fields_read.evidence: Ethernet, IP, and TCP header fields are stripped before feature extraction.

ech_considered.evidence: Specifically, we remove or randomize metadata features that may be unavailable in TLS 1.3 or ECH-enabled environments.

model_family.evidence: We propose a unified contrastive-learning-based framework, BoNC, capable of multi-class classification and discovery of novel botnet families in encrypted traffic.

split_protocols.evidence: Each dataset is randomly partitioned into training, validation, and testing subsets in an 8:1:1 ratio.

main_split.evidence: Each dataset is randomly partitioned into training, validation, and testing subsets in an 8:1:1 ratio.

easy_vs_hard_reported.evidence: From the complete family set of each benchmark, we sample two non-overlapping subsets: a labelled partition Cl used for supervised training and an unseen partition Cu reserved exclusively for evaluation.

shortcut_check.evidence: More details regarding the mask ratio is provided in ablation study (Section VI).

metrics.evidence: We report three metrics: accuracy on labeled classes, clustering accuracy on novel classes, and overall accuracy across all classes.

granularity.evidence: BoNC integrates into an online NIDS using sliding windows and incremental updates, maintaining a rolling buffer of T packets per active flow

first_n_packets.evidence: BoNC contains about 62 M parameters and requires roughly 4.1×108FLOPs per flow window of T=8 packets

cost_reported.evidence: and a throughput of approximately 165 flows/s (6.1 ms per flow).

hardware.evidence: We measured the compute footprint of BoNC and two representative baselines, TrafficFormer and YaTC, on the same hardware setup (Ubuntu 20.04, PyTorch 2.4.1 with CUDA 12.1, two NVIDIA A100 GPUs).
